memory_update.text: AXTI should be retained for Layer 2 because it maps directly to the InP substrate chokepoint; key survival tests are AI-specific InP revenue, export permits, capacity expansion, and customer qualification evidence.

AEHR should be retained as the optical-test/burn-in capacity candidate; survival depends on whether silicon-photonics orders broaden from lead-customer validation into repeat high-volume manufacturing demand.

POET should be carried as a speculative-shadow small-cap candidate for optical-interposer and external-light-source integration; require proof of production shipments, customer qualification, and revenue conversion before upgrading.

Reference-lane context for this node should continue to track AVGO, ANET, MRVL, NVDA, and major hyperscalers as demand anchors, but they should not crowd out Layer 1B discovery work on materials, lasers, optical engines, and test equipment.

Next pass should search US-listed or accessible ADR/OTC exposure to CW laser arrays, EML/DFB lasers, InP epi/wafers, optical inspection/metrology, connector/cable assemblies, and CPO supply-chain partners; Sivers is highly relevant but not US-listed common equity, so it needs a separate non-US/ADR treatment.

Reference-lane anchors remain Broadcom and Arista for AI networking demand context, but this pass prioritizes underfollowed US-listed suppliers closer to possible Serenity-style chokepoints: AXTI for InP substrates, AEHR for wafer-level burn-in/test of silicon-photonics devices, and POET for optical interposer/light-source integration.
